key_insight: The study reframes intrapartum fetal monitoring as a time-to-event prediction problem, enabling models to estimate both imminent delivery and fetal acidosis from continuous CTG signals.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help surface fetal distress risk earlier and more robustly during labor, rather than relying on a fixed pre-delivery window.
method: Deep discrete-time survival modeling for delivery timing
Marked point process modeling to jointly capture delivery and acidosis
Adapted to continuous physiologic signals with fully observed events and partially observed labels
evidence_signal: Marked DeepHit showed strong discrimination for delivery within one hour, with test AUROC of 0.837 at 6 hours and 0.935 at 12 hours into labor, and it also performed competitively near delivery on internal and external validation.
watch_item: Results are promising but require prospective validation before clinical use, especially because real-world deployment must handle label uncertainty and site-to-site differences in labor monitoring data.
paper_title: Deep Time-to-Event Models for Intrapartum Fetal Monitoring
